newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura to brief media on former president's arrest.
newsitem.headline: Nomura to brief media on former president's arrest.

text.p: Nomura Securities Co Ltd said on Friday that it would hold a news conference at 11 a.m. (0200 GMT) on the arrest of its former president Hideo Sakamaki.
Tokyo prosecutors said earlier that they had arrested Sakamaki on suspicion of conspiring with three Nomura executives to give 38.5 million yen to racketeer Ryuichi Koike in March 1995.

Sakamaki, who stepped down as president in March and is now an adviser to the leading brokerage, told a parliamentary panel this week that he briefly met Koike in 1992, but denied knowledge of any stock deals by Koike through Nomura.

Earlier this month, Japan's securities watchdog, the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission, filed a complaint with prosecutors against Nomura, two former Nomura executives and a company official alleging they had illegally compensated a firm run by Koike's younger brother Yoshinori.
The two former Nomura executives and the company official as well as the two Koike brothers are under arrest in connection with the case.
Sokaiya typically try to extort money from firms by threatening to expose dubious business practices or to make a disturbance at yearly shareholders' meetings -- called "sokai" in Japanese.
